draft.title: Literal and parameter equations
card: A parameter is a letter that stands for a fixed number whose value is not given, such as k in kx + 2 = 3. The unknown to solve for is x.
Collect the x terms and write the equation as ax = b, where a and b may involve k. Then check whether a is zero before dividing.
if a ≠ 0, divide to get x = b/a. For kx + 2 = 3, we get kx = 1, so x = 1/k when k ≠ 0.
if a = 0, the equation becomes 0 = b. If b ≠ 0 it is false for every x, so there is no solution. If b = 0 it is true for every x, so there are infinitely many.
draft.remember: Write ax = b. Only divide by a when a ≠ 0. If a = 0, look at b.

a.q: For which value of k does kx + 2 = 3 have no solution?
a.why: Rearranging gives kx = 1. If k = 0 this becomes 0 = 1, which is false for every x, so there is no solution. For k = 1, 2 or 3 we can divide by k and get one solution.
a.clue: Which value of k makes you unable to divide?

b.q: For which value of m does the equation 3x + 5 = mx + 5 have infinitely many solutions?
b.why: Collecting x terms gives (3 − m)x = 0. If m = 3 this is 0 = 0, which is true for every x. If m = 0 the equation is 3x = 0, which has the single solution x = 0.
b.clue: Make the x coefficient zero, then check what is left on the right.

final.title: Literal and parameter equations
card: A parameter is a letter that stands for a fixed number whose value is not given, such as \(k\) in \(kx + 2 = 3\). The unknown to solve for is \(x\).
Collect the \(x\) terms and write the equation as \(ax = b\), where \(a\) and \(b\) may involve \(k\). Then check whether \(a\) is zero before dividing.
if \(a \ne 0\), divide to get \(x = \frac{b}{a}\). For \(kx + 2 = 3\), we get \(kx = 1\), so \(x = \frac{1}{k}\) when \(k \ne 0\).
if \(a = 0\), the equation becomes \(0 = b\). If \(b \ne 0\) it is false for every \(x\), so there is no solution. If \(b = 0\) it is true for every \(x\), so there are infinitely many.
final.remember: Write \(ax = b\). Only divide by \(a\) when \(a \ne 0\). If \(a = 0\), look at \(b\).

a.q: For which value of \(k\) does \(kx + 2 = 3\) have no solution?
a.why: Rearranging gives \(kx = 1\). If \(k = 0\) this becomes \(0 = 1\), which is false for every \(x\), so there is no solution. For \(k = 1\), 2 or 3 we can divide by \(k\) and get one solution.
a.clue: Which value of \(k\) makes you unable to divide?

b.q: For which value of \(m\) does the equation \(3x + 5 = mx + 5\) have infinitely many solutions?
b.why: Collecting \(x\) terms gives \((3 - m)x = 0\). If \(m = 3\) this is \(0 = 0\), which is true for every \(x\). If \(m = 0\) the equation is \(3x = 0\), which has the single solution \(x = 0\).
b.clue: Make the \(x\) coefficient zero, then check what is left on the right.
